title: Respond to a patent demand letter
summary: Preserve the patent demand and relevant product evidence, identify the asserted patents and accused features, and have counsel assess scope, exposure and response options. Check available insurance or defense support and authorize the chosen response.

parts.title: Read what is actually asserted: the patent numbers, the accused features, the demanded license, and whether a claim chart maps claims to your product

execution.rationale: Extract the asserted patents, accused features, demands, and deadline from the supplied letter, and note whether a claim chart is present or needs to be requested.

parts.title: Preserve the evidence before anything changes: the letter, its dates, and the accused product's current behavior

execution.rationale: Archive the letter and capture the accused product's current state, versions, and documentation into a dated evidence file.

parts.title: If the letter asserts trademark, copyright, or other non-patent IP, run the cease-and-desist response instead

execution.rationale: The founder routes the letter to the matching playbook after reading what it asserts.

parts.title: Run the prior-art search: the asserted patents' prosecution histories, earlier filings, and products on sale before the priority dates

execution.rationale: Google Patents and USPTO Patent Public Search expose the asserted patents, their citations, and prior filings for a documented prior-art sweep; findings are inputs for counsel, not conclusions.

parts.title: Get patent counsel's read before any reply: the licensing-versus-fight economics are case math, not posture

execution.rationale: The founder and patent counsel weigh the asserted claims, the prior-art findings, and the defense and license costs for this specific letter.

parts.title: Check the escape hatches: existing IP or defense insurance, and memberships such as LOT Network or Unified Patents, before pricing a fight alone

execution.rationale: The founder reviews existing policies and membership options and talks to the insurer or network about coverage for this assertion.

parts.title: Pick the path on the letter's clock: license, negotiate, design around, or challenge validity

references.title: USPTO: Patent Trial and Appeal Board

geoResolutions.label: Validity can be challenged administratively: inter partes review at the PTAB is the standard route

execution.rationale: The founder decides with counsel among license, negotiation, design-around, and validity challenge, and answers within the letter's stated window.

parts.title: Wait out the counterparty: campaigns run in waves, and silence after a reply is common

execution.rationale: The founder monitors correspondence and docket activity on the assertion and keeps counsel informed of any follow-up.

metadata.trigger: A letter arrives asserting a patent against your product and demanding a license fee, often from a non-practicing entity (NPE).
metadata.supportReason: Letter parsing, evidence preservation, and the prior-art search are agent work; the counsel economics, the insurer and defense-fund conversations, and the path decision stay with people, and the counterparty answers on its own clock.

contextNeeded.query: the demand letter (patents asserted, accused features, deadline, any claim chart)
what the accused product actually does: versions, release dates, documentation

countryViews.title: Respond to a patent demand letter in United States
countryViews.summary: A patent demand letter is a business proposition dressed as a legal threat, and some are both. It is not a general cease-and-desist; that playbook is its own situation. Read what is actually asserted: the patent numbers, the accused features, and whether a claim chart maps claims to your product; if there is none, counsel's first ask is usually for one. Preserve the letter and the accused product's current behavior before anything changes. The economics are case math, stated plainly: a license can cost less than a month of defense, and a defense can cost less than a licensing campaign that repeats. Where patented products were not marked, damages ordinarily run only from when the infringer was notified (law rule us-fed.patent-marking-damages-notice), which is one reason the letter exists. Prior-art search is real work an agent can start the same day. Check your insurance and the defense-network memberships before pricing a fight alone. Then pick the path with patent counsel on the letter's clock. Educational guidance, not legal advice.
